parts.text: A student investigates the properties of a resistance wire. He uses the circuit shown in Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 3.1, draw a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference (p.d.) across length l of the resistance wire. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text: voltmeter in correct parallel connection and symbol correct

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) The student connects the crocodile clip to a length l = 20.0 cm of the resistance wire. He measures the value of potential difference V and current I for the resistance wire. Fig. 3.2 Fig. 3.3 Read, and record in the first line of Table 3.1, the values of V and I shown on the meters in Fig. 3.2 and Fig. 3.3. The student repeats the process for lengths l = 40.0 cm, l = 60.0 cm, l = 80.0 cm and l = 100.0 cm of the resistance wire in turn. His results are shown in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 l / cm V / V I / A R / Ω 20.0 40.0 1.7 0.47 3.6 60.0 2.2 0.52 4.2 80.0 2.3 0.35 6.6 100.0 2.4 0.29 8.3 [2]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) For length l = 20.0 cm, calculate and record in Table 3.1 the resistance R of the resistance wire. Use your values of V and I from (b)(i) and the equation R = V I . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Draw the straight line of best fit. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots
•
well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(d)(i)
ms.text: G present and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The gradient G is numerically equal to the resistance per unit length R 0 of the resistance wire. Write down a value of R 0 for this experiment. R 0 = ............................................... Ω / cm [1]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
any one inherent source of inaccuracy e.g.:
difficult to position crocodile clip accurately /
inconsistent connection with crocodile clip /
resistance wire not uniform
